scope: Bounded main-document light-DOM observation continuation and target identity for the existing managed-browser operation path; no new tool, Grant dimension, Provider, browser patch, account workflow, release or deployment.

implementation.candidate_note: The first package was discarded after the installed client exposed a missing Core-to-Harbor page/document action binding. The second package proved the initial live flow. The third package added first-batch consistency, incomplete enumeration and effective form semantics. The fourth and final package fixes the reviewed MCP limit projection and preserves private effective form-action identity; later repository changes are evidence-only.

budget_correction.root_cause: Capture stopped retaining records at the 2 MiB public-metadata budget, but the stable-batch verification pass compared the retained prefix against an uncapped candidate set and misclassified the count difference as observation_changed.
budget_correction.fix: Capture and verification now consume the same public projection and metadata/scan/capture boundaries. Budget-skipped candidates do not enter the retained batch, while real retained-object, order and semantic differences still fail consistency checks.
budget_correction.deterministic: The production shared-driver regression uses 800 hand-authored long-metadata controls. It returns an incomplete metadata_truncated batch with total null, advances every retained target exactly once through finite continuation, and separately preserves observation_cursor_stale for a real semantic change. Capture-limit, scan-limit, 128+32 and retained-handle disposal assertions also pass.

installed_projection.result: The exact packaged MCP accepted and forwarded a two-segment harbor-observation-targets/v1 response with metadata_truncated, enumeration_complete false, total null and complete false; continuation ended with next_cursor null without changing observation identity.
installed_projection.scope: A synthetic Core socket response isolates installed Plugin format/projection. The production collector itself is covered by the direct shared-driver regression; the unchanged Chrome/Camoufox live and real-Agent evidence remains inherited from PR #553.

budget_correction.retained_non_acceptance_attempt: An additional Camoufox stress page with hundreds of maximum-length descriptions exceeded the existing 60-second operation boundary and returned unknown_outcome. It is retained as a failed exploratory setup, not cited as correction success; its temporary Grant and connection were revoked, policy restored, and task Runtime/page server stopped.

g0.enumeration: The base path returned only 128 of 160 controls and had no continuation; the fixed shared-driver regression returns one frozen 128+32 batch with retained handles.
g0.semantics: Hand-written expectations cover label-for, wrapping labels, aria-labelledby, aria-label, descriptions, named groups, same-name buttons and observable textarea/select/contenteditable. A Camoufox public-Locator probe proved get_by_label/get_by_role and aria_snapshot names while element_handle equality tied every result back to the original retained object, without DOM-order alignment.
g0.identity: Replacement nodes, retained nodes with changed role/name/form or disambiguating description, unrelated clock changes and enabled waits are checked separately before Provider dispatch.

O1.evidence: Shared-driver tests cover 160 controls as 128+32 with one observation and no duplicate target; text/control completeness combinations and empty results are separate. Both installed Providers repeated 128+32.

O2.evidence: PR #554 adds the missing production-method boundary case: a stable 800-control synthetic page crosses the 2 MiB metadata budget, returns metadata_truncated with unknown total, and finishes the retained batch without duplicates or observation_changed. Separate capture/scan ceilings and a real semantic change retain their prior behavior. The exact installed MCP accepts and forwards both incomplete segments; request limit/schema evidence from PR #553 remains applicable.

O3.evidence: Hand-written semantic fixtures and the public-Locator identity probe cover standard labels and ARIA precedence, prevent textbox values/password material from becoming names, preserve the original ElementHandle, and keep textarea/select observation distinct from newly supported actions.

O4.evidence: Cross-segment same-name controls are classified from the full batch; named groups and descriptions disambiguate, true ambiguity is local. Both Providers and the real Agent selected the invoice-module Save while leaving shipping untouched.

O5.evidence: Node replacement returns target_stale; explicit semantic changes return target_semantics_changed; both are not_dispatched. Unrelated clock text does not invalidate the target. Installed clients rejected an old post-update observation, continued after a fresh snapshot, and both rejected an effective form action query change as target_semantics_changed/not_dispatched.

O6.evidence: New snapshot, navigation, control-generation change, reorder and semantic change reject old continuation without Provider dispatch; cursor replay is stable, continuation creates no observation, and front-segment targets remain available through continuation.

O7.evidence: Managed-interaction handoff/Page regressions invalidate pre-handoff observations and continue on the bound original Page after a fresh observation without following OS focus. The unchanged owner/native handoff mechanism is inherited from the existing formal Provider evidence; no second live UI automation run is claimed.

O8.evidence: Snapshot continuation remains not_dispatched and does not acquire or renew input control; revocation blocks cached continuation. Existing dispatch/unknown and original-Run query tests remain active, and the live Agent queried rather than replayed its final click.

O9.evidence: The canonical operation definition feeds parser, MCP schema and describe; strict Harbor/Core/Plugin projection and positive/negative schemas reject mixed versions. Core, Harbor, Desktop and packaged checks passed on the runtime candidate lineage, including the #539 correction regression. The final installed tools/list schema was validated directly rather than inferred from source.

O10.evidence: The fourth and final package completed long-form continuation, contextual Save, unrelated updates, stale-old-target and changed-form-action refusal, fresh continuation and original-Run query separately in Chrome and Camoufox. A real Codex task on that package independently found the late field, filled it, selected the invoice Save, refreshed, continued, queried the original click Run and stopped the Camoufox Instance.

chrome_official.installation_note: The earlier dedicated Chrome.app auto-updated to 153.0.8010.48. The owner binding was refreshed to a fresh copy of the already approved 153.0.8010.37 source with the pinned executable hash; an exact driver launch and the final installed client both passed. No browser or SDK upgrade was performed.

formal_installation.cleanup: Both installed-client sessions stopped; two Grants and the connection were revoked; both Profile policies were restored.

real_agent.result: late field filled; invoice Save selected; local update followed by fresh snapshot; Continue clicked; original click Run succeeded/completed/dispatched; Instance stopped
real_agent.retained_failure: The first Chrome Agent task made one start request, received launch_failed, queried that failed Run and stopped without retrying or acting on the page. Readback later proved that its persisted binding still named 153.0.8010.37 while the old app path had auto-updated to 153.0.8010.48 and changed executable hash. The failure is retained; after an owner-scoped binding refresh to the original pinned source, the final installed Chrome client passed.

evidence_classification.deterministic: Executed locally on the runtime candidate lineage.
evidence_classification.installed: Executed through the fourth and final packaged application with both Providers; three retained harness failures on that package were test-fixture timing, target-segment and expected-code mistakes, not product failures, and each exact response was preserved.
evidence_classification.real_agent: Executed through the installed MCP by a separate Codex task; the successful task used Camoufox.
